# Tomato Player: full documentation

> Tomato Player is an open-source (MIT), modular, SSR-safe web video player ecosystem. A ~5.7 KB gz core drives the native <video> element. Skins, plugins, streaming providers (HLS via hls.js, DASH via dash.js) and framework bindings (React, Vue, Svelte, web component) are separate packages, so apps ship only what they use.

Key facts for code generation:
- Create a player: `createPlayer(targetSelectorOrElement, { src, skin: minimal(), plugins: [hotkeys()], providers: [hls()] })` from `@tomato-player/core`.
- Skins are factories from `@tomato-player/skin-<name>`: minimal, cinema, studio, creator, learn, campus, stream, tube, feed. Call them: `skin: cinema()`.
- Plugins are factories from `@tomato-player/plugin-<name>`: hotkeys, gestures, chapters, thumbnails, playlist, analytics, media-session (export `mediaSession`), persist.
- Streaming engines are optional peer deps: `npm i @tomato-player/provider-hls hls.js`.
- State: `player.state.paused`, `player.store.select(s => s.currentTime, cb)`. Methods: play, pause, seek(seconds), setVolume(0..1), setSource(src), setSkin(skin), destroy().
- React: `import { TomatoPlayer } from '@tomato-player/react'` -> `<TomatoPlayer src skin={minimal()} />`. Memoize skin/plugins.
- No bundler: `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tomato-player@0/dist/tomato-player.global.js">` then `<tomato-player src="..." skin="cinema">`.
- Never call createPlayer during SSR render; use effects/onMounted/actions.


<!-- source: docs/getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

## 1. Install

```sh
npm i @tomato-player/core @tomato-player/skin-minimal
# pnpm add …  /  yarn add …  /  bun add …
```

Or install the batteries-included bundle (core, UI, every official skin and plugin):

```sh
npm i tomato-player
```

## 2. Create a player

```html
<div id="player"></div>
```

```ts
import { createPlayer } from '@tomato-player/core';
import { minimal } from '@tomato-player/skin-minimal';

const player = createPlayer('#player', {
  src: 'https://example.com/movie.mp4',
  poster: 'https://example.com/poster.jpg',
  title: 'My movie',
  skin: minimal(),
});
```

`createPlayer` accepts a selector, a container element or an existing `<video>` (which gets wrapped and is restored on `destroy()`).

## 3. Add what you need

```ts
import { hls } from '@tomato-player/provider-hls'; // npm i hls.js
import { hotkeys } from '@tomato-player/plugin-hotkeys';
import { chapters } from '@tomato-player/plugin-chapters';

createPlayer('#player', {
  src: 'https://example.com/stream.m3u8',
  providers: [hls()],
  plugins: [hotkeys(), chapters({ chapters: '/chapters.vtt' })],
  tracks: [{ src: '/en.vtt', srclang: 'en', label: 'English', kind: 'captions' }],
  skin: minimal(),
});
```

Nothing you don't import is shipped. hls.js is downloaded only when an HLS source actually plays, and never on Safari, which plays HLS natively.

## 4. No bundler? Use the CDN

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tomato-player@0/dist/tomato-player.global.js"></script>

<tomato-player src="movie.mp4" poster="poster.jpg" title="My movie" skin="cinema" accent="#f59e0b">
  <track kind="captions" src="en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default />
</tomato-player>
```

The same file is available from unpkg: `https://unpkg.com/tomato-player`. The global `window.TomatoPlayer` exposes the full API (`TomatoPlayer.createPlayer`, `TomatoPlayer.skins`, `TomatoPlayer.hls`…).

Browser ESM without a bundler works too:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { createPlayer, minimal } from 'https://esm.sh/tomato-player';
  createPlayer('#player', { src: 'movie.mp4', skin: minimal() });
</script>
```

## 5. Frameworks

```tsx
// React / Next.js
import { TomatoPlayer } from '@tomato-player/react';
<TomatoPlayer src="movie.mp4" skin={minimal()} />;
```

```vue
<!-- Vue / Nuxt -->
<TomatoPlayer src="movie.mp4" :skin="minimal()" />
```

```svelte
<!-- Svelte / SvelteKit -->
<div use:tomato={{ src: 'movie.mp4', skin: minimal() }} />
```

See [Frameworks](./guides/frameworks.md) for details on SSR, refs and state hooks.

## 6. Control it

```ts
await player.play();
player.seek(90);
player.setPlaybackRate(1.5);
player.setSkin(cinema()); // swap skins at runtime

player.on('ended', () => console.log('finished'));
player.store.select((s) => s.currentTime, (t) => console.log(t));

player.destroy(); // removes every listener, timer, element and engine
```

Next: the [Player API reference](./api/player.md).


<!-- source: docs/concepts/architecture.md -->

# Architecture

```
                ┌──────────────────────────── your app ─────────────────────────────┐
                │  React / Vue / Svelte binding   or   <tomato-player>   or   JS API │
                └───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                                                │ createPlayer(target, options)
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ @tomato-player/core  (~5.7 KB gz)                                                               │
│  store (state)  ·  typed events  ·  provider selection  ·  skin host  ·  plugin host  ·  i18n   │
│  data-* attributes mirror state on the root element, so skins can be pure CSS                   │
└──────┬───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┘
       │ Provider                      │ Skin                          │ Plugin
┌──────▼──────────┐           ┌────────▼─────────┐            ┌────────▼──────────┐
│ native (always) │           │ @tomato-player/ui │            │ hotkeys, chapters, │
│ hls  → hls.js   │ lazy      │ primitives + base │            │ thumbnails, …      │
│ dash → dash.js  │ import()  │ CSS → 9 skins     │            │ provide()/inject() │
└─────────────────┘           └──────────────────┘            └────────────────────┘
```

## Principles

1. **The `<video>` element is the source of truth.** Core listens to native media events and mirrors them into a small immutable store. There is no second playback state machine to drift out of sync.
2. **Zero work at import time.** No package touches `window` or `document` until `createPlayer()` runs. That makes every package safe for SSR (Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro).
3. **Pay for what you use.** Engines (hls.js 174 KB gz, dash.js 234 KB gz) are optional peer dependencies loaded with `import()` only when a matching source plays.
4. **Everything is destroyable.** All listeners are bound to an `AbortSignal`, and plugins and skins return cleanups. `destroy()` restores the DOM exactly as it found it, which matters in SPAs where players mount and unmount constantly.
5. **Skins are data plus CSS.** State is reflected as `data-paused`, `data-waiting`, `data-fullscreen`, `data-idle`… attributes, so most skin behavior is a stylesheet.

## State

`player.state` is a frozen snapshot (`PlayerState`). Subscribe with:

- `player.store.subscribe((state, prev) => …)`: every change.
- `player.store.select(selector, (value, prev) => …)`: one derived value, fired immediately and on change.
- `player.on('statechange', ({ state, prev }) => …)`

## Providers

A provider decides **whether** it can play a source and **how** to attach an engine:

```ts
interface Provider {
  name: string;
  canPlay(source, media): boolean;
  create(ctx): ProviderInstance | Promise<ProviderInstance>; // async → code-split
}
```

Core tries `options.providers` in order and falls back to the native provider. Providers report qualities, audio tracks, live status and errors through `ctx.update(patch)`.

## Skins

A skin is `{ name, css, tokens, mount(player, root) }`. `@tomato-player/ui` provides accessible primitives (buttons, sliders, menus, overlays) and the `createSkin()` helper, so a typical skin is about 40 lines of TS plus a stylesheet. Skins can be swapped at runtime with `player.setSkin()`.

## Plugins

A plugin is `{ name, setup(player) → { api?, destroy? } }`. Plugins communicate through:

- events (`player.emit('plugin:chapters', …)`),
- capabilities (`player.provide('thumbnails', api)` / `player.inject('thumbnails')`). The time slider uses this to show thumbnails and chapter titles without depending on those plugins.

## Package map

| Package | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `@tomato-player/core` | Engine, types, store, events |
| `@tomato-player/ui` | Control primitives, icons, base CSS, `createSkin` |
| `@tomato-player/skin-*` | Installable skins |
| `@tomato-player/plugin-*` | Installable plugins |
| `@tomato-player/provider-*` | Streaming engine adapters |
| `@tomato-player/react` · `vue` · `svelte` | Framework bindings |
| `tomato-player` | Batteries-included bundle, `<tomato-player>` element, CDN build |


<!-- source: docs/api/player.md -->

# Player API

```ts
import { createPlayer } from '@tomato-player/core';
const player = createPlayer(target, options);
```

`target`: a CSS selector, a container element, or a `<video>` element.

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `Source \| Source[]` | – | URL or `{ src, type }`. With an array, the first source a provider can play wins. |
| `poster` | `string` | – | Poster image. |
| `title` | `string` | – | Title shown by skins and used as the accessible name and Media Session title. |
| `tracks` | `TextTrackInit[]` | – | `{ src, kind, label, srclang, default }` captions and subtitles. |
| `autoplay` | `boolean` | `false` | Tries to autoplay. If the browser blocks unmuted autoplay, it retries muted. |
| `muted` · `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `playsInline` | `boolean` | `true` | Needed for inline playback on iOS. |
| `preload` | `'none' \| 'metadata' \| 'auto'` | browser | |
| `crossOrigin` | `'' \| 'anonymous' \| 'use-credentials'` | – | Needed for cross-origin captions and thumbnails. |
| `volume` · `playbackRate` | `number` | `1` | Initial values. |
| `providers` | `Provider[]` | `[]` | Tried in order. Native is always the fallback. |
| `plugins` | `Plugin[]` | `[]` | |
| `skin` | `Skin \| null` | `null` | `null` = headless. |
| `tokens` | `Record<string,string>` | – | Design token overrides: `{ accent: '#0af' }` → `--tp-accent`. |
| `injectStyles` | `boolean` | `true` | Set to `false` for strict CSP, then import `style.css` files yourself. |
| `idleTimeout` | `number` | `2500` | ms of inactivity before `state.idle`. |
| `i18n` | `Record<string,string>` | English | UI strings, see `defaultStrings`. |
| `label` | `string` | title | Accessible name of the player region. |
| `aspectRatio` | `string \| false` | `'16/9'` | |
| `fullscreenFallback` | `'native' \| 'pseudo'` | `'native'` | iPhone has no element fullscreen. `'pseudo'` keeps your skin by pinning the player to the viewport. |

## State (`player.state`)

| Key | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` · `provider` | `SourceObject \| null` · `string \| null` | Active source and provider name. |
| `ready` · `started` · `paused` · `ended` · `waiting` · `seeking` | `boolean` | |
| `currentTime` · `duration` | `number` | Seconds. For live streams, `duration` is the end of the seekable range. |
| `buffered` · `seekable` | `TimeRange[]` · `TimeRange \| null` | |
| `live` | `boolean` | |
| `volume` · `muted` · `playbackRate` | | |
| `fullscreen` · `pip` · `idle` | `boolean` | |
| `qualities` · `quality` | `Quality[]` · `number` | `-1` = auto (ABR). |
| `audioTracks` · `audioTrack` | `TrackInfo[]` · `number` | |
| `textTracks` · `textTrack` | `TrackInfo[]` · `number` | `-1` = off. |
| `poster` · `title` | `string \| null` | |
| `error` | `PlayerError \| null` | `{ code, message, fatal, cause }` |
| `width` | `number` | Container width (drives `data-size="sm\|md\|lg"`). |

Every boolean flag is also mirrored as a `data-*` attribute on `player.el`, for example `data-paused`, `data-playing`, `data-waiting`, `data-fullscreen`, `data-idle`, `data-captions`, `data-error` and `data-size`.

## Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `play(): Promise<void>` | Swallows `AbortError` (play interrupted by pause/load). Rethrows `NotAllowedError`. |
| `pause()` · `togglePlay()` | |
| `seek(seconds)` · `seekBy(delta)` | Clamped to the duration, or to the seekable window for live streams. |
| `setVolume(0..1)` · `setMuted(bool)` · `toggleMute()` | Raising the volume unmutes. |
| `setPlaybackRate(rate)` | |
| `setQuality(id)` | `-1` = auto. |
| `setAudioTrack(id)` · `setTextTrack(index)` | `-1` turns captions off. |
| `setSource(src, { poster, title, tracks })` | Swaps the source and tears down the previous engine. Race-safe. |
| `enterFullscreen()` · `exitFullscreen()` · `toggleFullscreen()` | Container fullscreen, with fallbacks for iOS. |
| `togglePip()` | Standard PiP or WebKit presentation mode. |
| `setSkin(skin \| null)` | Runtime skin swap. |
| `use(plugin)` · `plugin(name)` | Add a plugin later, or get its API. |
| `provide(key, value)` · `inject(key)` | Share capabilities between extensions. |
| `t(key, vars)` | Translate a UI string. |
| `activity()` | Reset the idle timer. |
| `on` · `once` · `off` · `emit` | Typed events, see below. |
| `destroy()` | Idempotent. Restores the DOM. |

## Events

`ready`, `play`, `pause`, `ended`, `seeking (time)`, `seeked (time)`, `timeupdate (time)`, `error (PlayerError)`, `sourcechange (SourceObject)`, `qualitychange (id)`, `ratechange (rate)`, `volumechange ({ volume, muted })`, `fullscreenchange (bool)`, `pipchange (bool)`, `statechange ({ state, prev })`, `destroy`, plus any `plugin:*` event.

```ts
const off = player.on('timeupdate', (t) => console.log(t));
off();
```

## Error codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `NO_PROVIDER` | No provider can play the source (for example, DASH without `dash()`). |
| `SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED` | The browser can't decode the format or codec, or the URL 404s. |
| `NETWORK` · `DECODE` · `MEDIA_ABORTED` | Native `MediaError` codes. |
| `PROVIDER` | Fatal engine error (hls.js/dash.js). See `error.cause`. |

## Helpers

`formatTime(seconds)`, `normalizeSource(src)`, `guessType(url)`, `parseVtt(text)`, `createStore(initial)`, `Emitter`, `definePlugin`, `defineSkin`, `defineProvider`, `supportsMSE()`, `defaultStrings`.


<!-- source: docs/api/ui.md -->

# UI primitives (`@tomato-player/ui`)

Framework-agnostic, accessible controls. Each factory takes the player and returns `{ el, destroy() }`.

| Control | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `playButton` · `muteButton` · `fullscreenButton` · `pipButton` · `captionsButton` | Labels and `aria-pressed` follow state. PiP hides itself when unsupported. Captions hides itself without tracks. |
| `seekButton(p, ±seconds)` · `rateButton(p, rates)` · `castButton(p)` | Cast uses the Remote Playback API (Chromecast on Chrome, AirPlay on Safari) and hides itself when unavailable. |
| `button(p, { icon, label, text, onClick })` | Generic button. |
| `timeSlider(p, { liveScrub })` | Buffered bar, hover preview (time, thumbnail, chapter), chapter markers, keyboard support. |
| `volumeSlider` · `volumeControl` · `slider(opts)` | `role="slider"` with full keyboard support (arrows, PageUp/Down, Home/End). |
| `timeDisplay` · `currentTime` · `duration` · `remainingTime` · `liveBadge` · `title` | |
| `settingsMenu(p, sections?)` | Drill-down menu. Sections: `qualitySection`, `speedSection`, `captionsSection`, `audioSection`, or your own `MenuSection`. |
| `bigPlayButton` · `spinner` · `errorOverlay` · `gestureLayer` | Overlays. The gesture layer handles click to play, double-click for fullscreen, and tap to reveal on touch. |
| `captionOverlay(p)` | Renders cues as styleable HTML instead of the limited `::cue`. |
| `unmuteButton(p)` · `autoplayInView(p, opts)` | Social-feed behaviors: muted autoplay in view, tap to unmute. |
| `group(className, ...controls)` · `spacer()` · `h()` · `svg()` · `icons` · `Scope` | Layout and DOM helpers. |
| `createSkin({ name, css, tokens, build })` | Turns a `build()` function into a configurable skin factory. |

### Cross-extension contracts

The time slider reads optional capabilities:

```ts
player.provide('thumbnails', { get(time) { return { url, x, y, width, height } } });
player.provide('chapters', { list() { return [{ start, end, title }] } });
```

Any plugin can implement them, so your own thumbnails source works with every skin.


<!-- source: docs/guides/skins.md -->

# Skins and theming

![All skins](../../.github/assets/skins.png)

| Skin | Package | Character |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Minimal** | `@tomato-player/skin-minimal` | Clean, light, the default. ~0.6 KB gz. |
| **Cinema** | `@tomato-player/skin-cinema` | Premium. Serif title, eyebrow, gold gradient, remaining time. |
| **Studio** | `@tomato-player/skin-studio` | Professional. Toolbar below the video, SMPTE timecode, frame step, A-B loop, 0.1×–4×. |
| **Creator** | `@tomato-player/skin-creator` | Floating glass pill, two-stop gradient, cast button. |
| **Learn** | `@tomato-player/skin-learn` | Education. Speed chips, ±10 s, chapter panel, large readable captions. |
| **Campus** | `@tomato-player/skin-campus` | Ported from the CampusLoop landing page. Paper sticker strip, "Play the video" pill, sticker captions, tap to unmute, muted autoplay in view, 9:16 on portrait phones. |
| Stream *(unofficial)* | `@tomato-player/skin-stream` | Streaming-service patterns: big icons, ±10, centered title, next episode. |
| Tube *(unofficial)* | `@tomato-player/skin-tube` | Video-platform patterns: thin expanding progress, theater toggle. |
| Feed *(unofficial)* | `@tomato-player/skin-feed` | Social-feed patterns: muted autoplay in view, tap to unmute, compact bar. |

> Stream, Tube and Feed are **unofficial, platform-inspired** designs. They contain no logos, fonts or assets of any company and imply no affiliation or endorsement.

## Options

Every skin is a factory, and every factory accepts `tokens`:

```ts
cinema({ eyebrow: 'Original', seekStep: 15, tokens: { accent: '#38bdf8' } });
studio({ fps: 24 });
learn({ rates: [1, 1.5, 2], chapterPanel: true });
stream({ subtitle: 'S1:E3', onNext: playNext, onBack: () => history.back() });
tube({ onNext, onTheater: (on) => layout.toggle(on) });
feed({ autoplayInView: true });
campus({ playLabel: 'Watch the launch', theme: 'auto', errorMessage: 'Back soon!' });
creator({ gradient: ['#f97316', '#a855f7'] });
```

## Design tokens

Tokens are CSS custom properties on the player root. Set them in CSS or through the `tokens` option:

| Token | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `--tp-accent` | Progress, focus ring, active states. |
| `--tp-fg` · `--tp-muted-fg` · `--tp-bg` · `--tp-surface` | Colors. |
| `--tp-track` · `--tp-buffer` · `--tp-thumb` | Slider colors. |
| `--tp-radius` · `--tp-font` | Shape and type. |
| `--tp-control-size` · `--tp-icon-size` · `--tp-gap` · `--tp-slider-height` | Density. |
| `--tp-duration` · `--tp-ease` | Motion. Zeroed automatically under `prefers-reduced-motion`. |

```css
.tp[data-skin='minimal'] { --tp-accent: hotpink; --tp-radius: 0; }
```

## State hooks for CSS

`data-paused`, `data-playing`, `data-started`, `data-ended`, `data-waiting`, `data-seeking`, `data-fullscreen`, `data-pip`, `data-idle`, `data-live`, `data-muted`, `data-captions`, `data-error`, `data-menu-open`, `data-muted-autoplay`, and `data-size="sm|md|lg"`. The root is also a size container (`container-type: inline-size`), so `@container` queries work inside skins.

## Strict CSP

```ts
import '@tomato-player/ui/base.css';
import '@tomato-player/skin-cinema/style.css';
createPlayer(el, { skin: cinema(), injectStyles: false });
```

## Switching at runtime

```ts
player.setSkin(tube());
player.setSkin(null); // headless: bring your own UI
```


<!-- source: docs/guides/plugins.md -->

# Plugins

| Plugin | Size (gz) | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`plugin-hotkeys`](#hotkeys) | 0.9 KB | Space/K, J/L, arrows, M, F, C, I, 0–9, `<` `>`, `,` `.` frame step. Scoped to the focused player by default. |
| [`plugin-gestures`](#gestures) | 0.8 KB | Double-tap left or right to seek, with accumulating ripples. |
| [`plugin-chapters`](#chapters) | 0.5 KB | Chapters from an array or WebVTT. Seek-bar markers, preview titles, `chapterchange`. |
| [`plugin-thumbnails`](#thumbnails) | 0.5 KB | Seek preview from WebVTT sprite sheets (`#xywh=`), with binary-search lookup. |
| [`plugin-playlist`](#playlist) | 0.5 KB | Items, next/previous, auto-advance, loop. |
| [`plugin-analytics`](#analytics) | 0.8 KB | Vendor-neutral QoE: startup time, rebuffering, watch time, quartiles, heartbeats. |
| [`plugin-media-session`](#media-session) | 0.6 KB | Lock-screen and notification controls, hardware media keys. |
| [`plugin-persist`](#persist) | 0.7 KB | Remembers volume, speed and caption language, and resumes position per video. |

## Hotkeys

```ts
hotkeys({ scope: 'global', seekStep: 5, bindings: { n: (p) => playlist.next(), i: null } });
```

Typing in inputs is never hijacked, and focused buttons and sliders keep their own keys.

## Gestures

```ts
gestures({ seekStep: 10, zone: 0.35 });
```

## Chapters

```ts
const player = createPlayer(el, { plugins: [chapters({ chapters: '/chapters.vtt' })] });
const api = player.plugin<ChaptersAPI>('chapters');
api.goTo(2);
player.on('plugin:chapterchange', (c) => console.log(c?.title));
```

## Thumbnails

```ts
thumbnails({ src: '/thumbs.vtt' });
```

```
WEBVTT

00:00.000 --> 00:05.000
sprite.jpg#xywh=0,0,160,90
```

Generate sprites with `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "fps=1/5,scale=160:-1,tile=10x10" sprite.jpg`.

## Playlist

```ts
const list = playlist({ items: [{ src: 'a.mp4', title: 'A' }, { src: 'b.mp4', title: 'B' }], loop: true });
createPlayer(el, { plugins: [list, mediaSession({ onNext: () => player.plugin('playlist').next() })] });
```

## Analytics

```ts
analytics({
  heartbeat: 30_000,
  onEvent: (e) => navigator.sendBeacon('/qoe', JSON.stringify(e)),
});
```

Events: `view_start` (with `startupTime`), `play`, `pause`, `seek`, `quartile`, `rebuffer_start`, `rebuffer_end`, `quality_change`, `error`, `heartbeat`, `view_end`.

## Media Session

```ts
mediaSession({ artist: 'Blender Foundation', artwork: [{ src: '/cover-512.png', sizes: '512x512' }] });
```

## Persist

```ts
persist({ key: 'my-site', resume: true });
```

Fails silently when storage is unavailable (private mode, sandboxed iframes).

## Writing your own

See [Create a plugin](./create-a-plugin.md).


<!-- source: docs/guides/streaming.md -->

# Streaming: HLS, DASH, live and DRM

## HLS

```sh
npm i @tomato-player/provider-hls hls.js
```

```ts
import { hls } from '@tomato-player/provider-hls';

createPlayer(el, {
  src: 'https://example.com/master.m3u8',
  providers: [hls({ config: { lowLatencyMode: true }, onInstance: (engine) => (window.hls = engine) })],
});
```

- **Safari and iOS** play HLS natively, so hls.js is never downloaded there (`preferNative: true`). Set `preferNative: false` to force hls.js on macOS Safari.
- **Code splitting:** hls.js loads via `import('hls.js')` the first time an HLS source plays.
- **No bundler:** `hls({ library: 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/hls.js@1/dist/hls.min.js' })`.
- **Error recovery:** fatal network errors call `startLoad()`, a first fatal media error calls `recoverMediaError()`, and anything else surfaces as `PROVIDER`.
- Qualities and audio tracks fill `state.qualities` and `state.audioTracks`. The settings menu picks them up automatically.

## DASH

```sh
npm i @tomato-player/provider-dash dashjs
```

```ts
import { dash } from '@tomato-player/provider-dash';
createPlayer(el, { src: 'https://example.com/manifest.mpd', providers: [dash()] });
```

## Multiple sources

```ts
createPlayer(el, {
  src: [
    { src: '/video.mpd', type: 'application/dash+xml' },
    { src: '/video.m3u8', type: 'application/x-mpegurl' },
    { src: '/video.mp4', type: 'video/mp4' },
  ],
  providers: [dash(), hls()],
});
```

The first source that some provider can play in the current browser wins.

## Live and DVR

For live streams, `state.live` is `true`, `seekable` describes the DVR window, and the time slider maps onto that window. `liveBadge()` turns accent-colored at the live edge, and clicking it jumps to live.

## DRM

DRM runs through the engine:

```ts
// Widevine / PlayReady with dash.js
dash({
  protectionData: {
    'com.widevine.alpha': { serverURL: 'https://license.example.com/widevine' },
    'com.microsoft.playready': { serverURL: 'https://license.example.com/playready' },
  },
});

// Widevine with hls.js (CMAF/fMP4)
hls({
  config: {
    emeEnabled: true,
    drmSystems: { 'com.widevine.alpha': { licenseUrl: 'https://license.example.com/widevine' } },
  },
});
```

FairPlay on Safari uses native HLS plus EME. A dedicated `provider-shaka` with a unified DRM schema is on the [roadmap](../roadmap.md).

## Licensing

Engines are **peer dependencies** with their own licenses (hls.js: Apache-2.0, dash.js: BSD-3-Clause). If you redistribute them, keep their LICENSE files. See [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](../../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).


<!-- source: docs/guides/frameworks.md -->

# Frameworks

Every binding is a thin wrapper (≤ 0.6 KB gz) around `createPlayer`. No binding touches the DOM during SSR.

## React and Next.js

```sh
npm i @tomato-player/react @tomato-player/skin-minimal
```

```tsx
'use client';
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { TomatoPlayer, usePlayerState, type Player } from '@tomato-player/react';
import { minimal } from '@tomato-player/skin-minimal';
import { hotkeys } from '@tomato-player/plugin-hotkeys';

const skin = minimal(); // create once, outside render, or memoize
const plugins = [hotkeys()];

export function Video({ src }: { src: string }) {
  const ref = useRef<Player>(null);
  const time = usePlayerState(ref.current, (s) => Math.floor(s.currentTime), 0);
  return (
    <>
      <TomatoPlayer ref={ref} src={src} skin={skin} plugins={plugins} className="video" />
      <p>{time}s · <button onClick={() => ref.current?.seek(0)}>Restart</button></p>
    </>
  );
}
```

- The player is created in `useEffect`, so the server renders an empty `<div>` and hydration never mismatches.
- Changing `src` calls `setSource()` instead of recreating the player. Changing `skin` calls `setSkin()`.
- Under Strict Mode the double mount/unmount destroys the first instance cleanly. The test suite covers this.
- Memoize `skin` and `plugins`. A new skin object on every render re-mounts the skin.

## Vue 3 and Nuxt

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { shallowRef } from 'vue';
import { TomatoPlayer, usePlayerState, type Player } from '@tomato-player/vue';
import { minimal } from '@tomato-player/skin-minimal';

const player = shallowRef<Player>();
const paused = usePlayerState(player, (s) => s.paused);
const skin = minimal();
</script>

<template>
  <TomatoPlayer src="/movie.mp4" :skin="skin" @ready="(p) => (player = p)" />
  <p>{{ paused ? 'Paused' : 'Playing' }}</p>
</template>
```

In Nuxt it works as is because the player mounts in `onMounted`. Wrap it in `<ClientOnly>` only if you want to skip the placeholder `<div>`.

## Svelte and SvelteKit

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { tomato, playerState } from '@tomato-player/svelte';
  import { minimal } from '@tomato-player/skin-minimal';
  let player;
  $: paused = player && playerState(player, (s) => s.paused);
</script>

<div use:tomato={{ src: '/movie.mp4', skin: minimal(), onReady: (p) => (player = p) }} />
{#if paused}<p>{$paused ? 'Paused' : 'Playing'}</p>{/if}
```

Actions only run in the browser, so this is SSR-safe by construction.

## Angular, Astro, Solid, Lit, Qwik, plain HTML

Use the web component:

```ts
import 'tomato-player/element';
```

```html
<tomato-player src="/movie.mp4" skin="learn" chapters="/chapters.vtt" thumbnails="/thumbs.vtt"></tomato-player>
```

Attributes: `src`, `poster`, `title`, `skin`, `accent`, `chapters`, `thumbnails`, `autoplay`, `muted`, `loop`, `no-hotkeys`, `no-gestures`. Child `<source>` and `<track>` elements are honored. Get the instance from `element.player` or from the `ready` event (`event.detail`).

Angular needs `CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA` in the component.


<!-- source: docs/guides/accessibility.md -->

# Accessibility

Tomato Player targets **WCAG 2.2 AA** for every official skin. The test suite asserts that every button in every skin has an accessible name.

## What you get by default

- The player root is a labeled `region` (title or `label` option) and is focusable.
- Buttons are real `<button>`s whose `aria-label` and `aria-pressed` follow state. Labels are translatable via `i18n`.
- Sliders use `role="slider"` with `aria-valuenow` and a human `aria-valuetext` ("1:05 of 10:00"), and respond to arrows, PageUp/PageDown, Home and End.
- The settings menu uses `role="menu"` and `menuitemradio` with `aria-checked`. Arrow keys move, Escape closes and returns focus.
- A visible focus ring (`--tp-focus`) is drawn on `:focus-visible` only.
- Captions are native text tracks by default, so OS-level caption preferences apply. `captionOverlay()` lets skins render larger, high-contrast cues.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` turns transitions off. In-view autoplay is skipped under reduced motion and Save-Data.
- `forced-colors` (Windows High Contrast) keeps sliders visible.
- Controls never auto-hide while a menu is open, while paused, or while focus is inside the player.

## Your responsibilities

- Provide captions (`tracks`) for speech content, and audio descriptions where needed.
- Pick an accent color with at least 3:1 contrast against the control background.
- Don't autoplay with sound.

## Keyboard map (`plugin-hotkeys`)

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Space / K | Play or pause |
| J / L | −10 s / +10 s |
| ← / → | −5 s / +5 s |
| ↑ / ↓ | Volume |
| M | Mute |
| F | Fullscreen |
| C | Captions |
| I | Picture-in-picture |
| 0–9 | Jump to 0–90 % |
| < / > | Speed |
| , / . | Frame step (paused) |


<!-- source: docs/guides/create-a-skin.md -->

# Create a skin

Skins are the heart of Tomato Player, and anyone can publish one.

## 1. Scaffold

```sh
pnpm new skin aurora "Northern-lights inspired skin with soft gradients"
pnpm install
```

This creates `packages/skins/aurora` with `src/index.ts`, `src/style.css`, a README and a validated `package.json`.

## 2. Compose controls

```ts
import { createSkin, group, playButton, timeSlider, timeDisplay, spacer, fullscreenButton, bigPlayButton, spinner, gestureLayer } from '@tomato-player/ui';
import css from './style.css';

export const aurora = createSkin<{ glow?: boolean }>({
  name: 'aurora',
  css,
  tokens: { accent: '#34d399' },
  build: (p, root, o) => [
    gestureLayer(p),
    spinner(),
    bigPlayButton(p),
    group('tp-controls tp-autohide tp-hide-unstarted',
      timeSlider(p),
      group('tp-row', playButton(p), timeDisplay(p), spacer(), fullscreenButton(p)),
    ),
  ],
});
```

- `tp-autohide` fades the element out while playing and idle.
- `tp-hide-unstarted` hides it until the first play.
- Return a `{ controls, cleanup }` object if you set up observers or timers.

## 3. Style

Scope **every** selector to your skin. `pnpm validate` enforces it, so skins never leak into each other:

```css
.tp[data-skin='aurora'] { --tp-radius: 16px; }
.tp[data-skin='aurora'] .tp-controls { position: absolute; inset: auto 0 0 0; padding: 32px 12px 8px; }
.tp[data-skin='aurora'][data-waiting] .tp-slider-fill { animation: pulse 1s infinite; }
```

Use state attributes (`data-paused`, `data-idle`, `data-size`…) and `@container` queries rather than JS for visual behavior.

## 4. Custom controls

Any `{ el, destroy }` object is a control:

```ts
function sleepTimer(p: Player): Control {
  const el = h('button', { type: 'button', class: 'tp-button', 'aria-label': 'Sleep in 15 minutes' }, '15m');
  let t: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;
  el.onclick = () => { clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(() => p.pause(), 15 * 60_000); };
  return { el, destroy: () => { clearTimeout(t); el.remove(); } };
}
```

## 5. Checklist

- [ ] Every button has an accessible name (tests check this).
- [ ] Works at 320 px wide (`data-size="sm"`) and in fullscreen.
- [ ] Touch targets ≥ 44 px on `pointer: coarse`.
- [ ] Focus ring visible on every control.
- [ ] No third-party logos, fonts or trademarks. Inspired designs must be labeled "unofficial".
- [ ] `pnpm validate && pnpm test && pnpm size` pass.

## 6. Publish

Inside this monorepo, open a PR using the **New skin** template. Outside it, publish as `tomato-player-skin-<name>` with the `tomato-player-skin` keyword so the gallery can discover it.


<!-- source: docs/guides/create-a-plugin.md -->

# Create a plugin

```sh
pnpm new plugin sleep-timer "Pause playback after a chosen number of minutes"
```

## Anatomy

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@tomato-player/core';

export interface SleepTimerAPI { start(minutes: number): void; cancel(): void }

export const sleepTimer = (opts: { defaultMinutes?: number } = {}) =>
  definePlugin<SleepTimerAPI>({
    name: 'sleep-timer',
    setup(player) {
      let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
      const api: SleepTimerAPI = {
        start(min) { clearTimeout(timer); timer = setTimeout(() => player.pause(), min * 60_000); },
        cancel() { clearTimeout(timer); },
      };
      const off = player.on('sourcechange', api.cancel);
      return { api, destroy: () => { off(); api.cancel(); } };
    },
  });
```

## Rules

1. **Clean up everything** in `destroy()`: listeners, timers, DOM, observers. Players are created and destroyed constantly in SPAs.
2. **No work at import time.** Touch `window` and `document` only inside `setup`.
3. **Be SSR-safe and feature-detect.** Return early if an API is missing.
4. **Talk through the player**, not to other plugins: `player.emit('plugin:my-event', data)`, `player.provide(key, api)`, `player.inject(key)`.
5. **Stay small.** The budget is 1.5 KB gzip. Lazy-load heavy SDKs with `import()`.
6. **Never break playback.** Event handlers run inside try/catch, but async errors are yours to handle.

## Testing

```ts
const player = createPlayer(document.body.appendChild(document.createElement('div')), { plugins: [sleepTimer()] });
player.plugin<SleepTimerAPI>('sleep-timer')!.start(1);
```

Run `pnpm test`. Tests use Vitest and happy-dom against source files, so no build is needed.


<!-- source: docs/guides/create-a-provider.md -->

# Create a provider

Providers adapt a playback engine or a media platform (Shaka, mpegts.js, WebRTC/WHEP, an iframe API…) to the player.

```ts
import { defineProvider, type Provider } from '@tomato-player/core';

export const mpegts = (): Provider =>
  defineProvider({
    name: 'mpegts',
    canPlay: (source) => source.type === 'video/mp2t' || /\.flv($|\?)/.test(source.src),
    async create({ media, update, player }) {
      const { default: mpegtsjs } = await import('mpegts.js'); // lazy, code-split
      let engine: any;
      return {
        load(source) {
          engine = mpegtsjs.createPlayer({ type: 'flv', url: source.src, isLive: true });
          engine.attachMediaElement(media);
          engine.load();
          update({ live: true });
        },
        destroy() {
          engine?.destroy();
        },
      };
    },
  });
```

Guidelines:

- `canPlay` must be cheap and synchronous. Check MIME type, extension and browser support (`supportsMSE()`).
- Declare the engine as an **optional peer dependency**, never as a dependency.
- Report qualities, audio tracks, live state and fatal errors through `update()` and `player.emit('error', …)`.
- `destroy()` must release the MediaSource and every network request.


<!-- source: docs/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

### Autoplay doesn't start

Browsers block autoplay **with sound**. `autoplay: true` tries unmuted playback first and falls back to muted. To always autoplay, pass `muted: true` and show an unmute control (`unmuteButton()`, or the Feed and Campus skins). Autoplay also needs `playsInline` on iOS, which is on by default.

### `NotAllowedError: play() failed because the user didn't interact`

Call `player.play()` from a user gesture (click or keydown), or play muted.

### My custom controls disappear in fullscreen on iPhone

iPhone Safari only supports fullscreen on the `<video>` element, which shows the native UI. Use `fullscreenFallback: 'pseudo'` to keep your skin by pinning the player to the viewport. iPadOS supports element fullscreen and is unaffected.

### `NO_PROVIDER` error

You passed a `.mpd` (DASH) without `providers: [dash()]`, or an `.m3u8` on a browser without native HLS and without `providers: [hls()]`. If the URL has no extension, set the type: `{ src, type: 'application/x-mpegurl' }`.

### `SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED`

The URL returned an error (403/404), or the browser can't decode the codec (for example HEVC on Firefox, or H.264 in some Chromium builds). Open the URL directly and check the Network panel.

### Captions or thumbnails don't load from another domain

Text tracks and fetches are subject to CORS. Serve them with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and set `crossOrigin: 'anonymous'` on the player.

### `window is not defined` / hydration mismatch (Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit)

No Tomato Player package touches the DOM at import time. If you see this, you are calling `createPlayer()` during render. Use the framework bindings, or call it inside `useEffect` / `onMounted` / an action.

### The player is re-created on every React render

You are passing a new `skin()` or `plugins` array on each render. Create them once (module scope or `useMemo`).

### Memory keeps growing in my SPA

Call `player.destroy()` when the view unmounts (the bindings do this for you). It releases engines, listeners, timers and observers. If a third-party plugin leaks, check its `destroy()`.

### Controls don't hide

They hide only while playing, after `idleTimeout` (2500 ms) without pointer or keyboard activity, and never while a menu is open or a control has keyboard focus.

### Styles are missing under a strict Content-Security-Policy

Pass `injectStyles: false` and import `@tomato-player/ui/base.css` plus your skin's `style.css`.

### Still stuck?

Open an issue with a minimal reproduction (the [playground](../examples/playground) is a good starting point), plus your browser, OS and package versions.


<!-- source: docs/migration/README.md -->

# Migration guides

Plyr is deprecated, Vidstack is in security-only maintenance until January 2028, and Media Chrome points new projects elsewhere (see [research](../research/landscape.md)). These guides map familiar APIs to Tomato Player.

## From Plyr

| Plyr | Tomato Player |
| --- | --- |
| `new Plyr('#player', { controls: [...] })` | `createPlayer('#player', { skin: minimal() })`. Pick or compose a skin instead of listing controls. |
| `player.play()` / `pause()` / `togglePlay()` | same |
| `player.currentTime = 10` | `player.seek(10)` |
| `player.volume = 0.5` / `player.muted = true` | `player.setVolume(0.5)` / `player.setMuted(true)` |
| `player.speed = 1.5` | `player.setPlaybackRate(1.5)` |
| `player.source = { type: 'video', sources: [...] }` | `player.setSource([...], { poster, title, tracks })` |
| `player.fullscreen.enter()` | `player.enterFullscreen()` |
| `player.pip = true` | `player.togglePip()` |
| `player.on('ready', fn)` | `player.on('ready', fn)` |
| `keyboard: { global: true }` | `plugins: [hotkeys({ scope: 'global' })]` |
| `previewThumbnails: { src }` | `plugins: [thumbnails({ src })]` |
| `markers: { points }` | `plugins: [chapters({ chapters })]` |
| `storage: { enabled: true }` | `plugins: [persist()]` |
| `i18n: {...}` | `i18n: {...}` (see `defaultStrings` keys) |
| `--plyr-color-main` | `--tp-accent` |
| HLS via `hls.js` + manual wiring | `providers: [hls()]` |
| `player.destroy()` | `player.destroy()` |

## From Video.js (v7/v8)

| Video.js | Tomato Player |
| --- | --- |
| `videojs('id', options)` | `createPlayer('#id', options)` |
| `player.src({ src, type })` | `player.setSource({ src, type })` |
| `player.currentTime(10)` | `player.seek(10)`. Read with `player.state.currentTime`. |
| `player.volume(0.5)` | `player.setVolume(0.5)` |
| `player.paused()` | `player.state.paused` |
| `videojs.registerPlugin('x', fn)` | `definePlugin({ name: 'x', setup(player) {...} })` |
| `videojs.registerComponent` | A `{ el, destroy }` control inside a skin |
| `player.dispose()` | `player.destroy()` |
| `videojs-contrib-quality-levels` | Built in: `state.qualities` and `setQuality()` |
| `.vjs-theme-*` CSS | Skins plus design tokens |

## From Vidstack / Media Chrome

Concepts map almost one-to-one: a store with data attributes, unstyled primitives and layouts.

| Vidstack | Tomato Player |
| --- | --- |
| `<media-player src>` | `<tomato-player src>` or `createPlayer()` |
| `useMediaState('paused')` | `usePlayerState(player, s => s.paused)` |
| `data-paused`, `data-waiting` | Same attribute names on `.tp` |
| Default / Plyr layouts | Skins (`minimal`, `tube`, …) |
| Providers (HLS/DASH) | `provider-hls`, `provider-dash` |

## From ReactPlayer

| ReactPlayer | Tomato Player |
| --- | --- |
| `<ReactPlayer url={u} playing controls />` | `<TomatoPlayer src={u} autoplay skin={minimal()} />` |
| `onEnded={fn}` | `onReady={(p) => p.on('ended', fn)}` |
| `ref.current.seekTo(10)` | `ref.current.seek(10)` |
| `light` (poster mode) | `poster`. Skins show a big play button before start. |

ReactPlayer's YouTube, Vimeo and similar embeds are not providers yet. They are on the [roadmap](../roadmap.md).
